children: The approval is subject to banking, foreign exchange and other applicable regulatory requirements

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved SBI Mutual Fund’s proposal to acquire an aggregate stake of up to 9.99 per cent in South Indian Bank, according to a regulatory filing by the private sector lender. The approval was communicated to the bank on 23 November 2026 and is subject to compliance with applicable regulatory conditions. The development comes after South Indian Bank reported a 21 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 426 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27, supported by improved margins and better asset quality.
South Indian Bank said the central bank had permitted SBI Mutual Fund to acquire an aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent of the bank’s paid-up share capital or voting rights.

The approval remains subject to the conditions specified by the RBI. The proposed acquisition must comply with the applicable legal and regulatory framework governing shareholding in commercial banks.
The approval is subject to the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the RBI’s Directions on Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights in Commercial Banks, 2025.

The transaction must also comply with the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, along with other applicable laws and regulatory guidelines. The bank’s filing did not specify a timeline for the proposed acquisition or the price at which the shares may be acquired.
South Indian Bank reported a net profit of Rs 426 crore for the second quarter of FY27, marking a 21 per cent increase compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.

The improvement was supported by stronger margins and better asset quality, according to the report. The latest earnings performance provides additional context to the regulatory development, although the bank has not indicated any direct link between the profit growth and the proposed acquisition by SBI Mutual Fund.

The RBI approval permits SBI Mutual Fund to acquire a holding of up to 9.99 per cent, subject to the specified conditions. The approval does not, by itself, confirm that the acquisition has been completed or that the fund will acquire the maximum permitted stake.
The eventual holding will depend on the fund’s acquisition decisions and compliance with the applicable regulatory requirements.
